convoLines.text: "Don't mind me. Today's just heavy."
They light up a little when they see you.
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
Sung won't meet your eyes. "I told myself finders keepers. It wasn't finders keepers. I'm sorry."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Sung rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"Between us — Heh. Nobody's asked me that in a while. ...I'm alright. Getting there."
"Ruth killed the things that come at night. I did too. That's a small club, and it's smaller now."
"I'd love to. Lead the way." (They're already checking your pack.)
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
Liam: "I've heard good things about The Red Table. We should link with them — we'd be stronger together."
They grin when they spot you — unguarded, for once.
"Good. What I've heard of them, I believe. Go and ask." You carry the proposal to The Red Table.
"I asked Pasquale about this wound — Pasquale's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"About this wound — I still haven't found anyone. Any chance?"
"It keeps getting worse. I can't haul or hunt with it like this — and if it festers, I'm done for. Please, clean it out and bind it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Anyway — that's my problem, not yours. What did you want?"
"Since Ruth died... I keep expecting to see Ruth at the fire. Stupid."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
"All right —" Sam starts to stand, then sinks back down. "Maybe not today. The fire's got me."
"I sleep with one ear uncovered, always the way Ruth used to, when they were the one keeping me steady. It doesn't work the same. I do it anyway."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Sung grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Sam is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Sung: "You. Yeah, you. What do you make of this?"
"Take your time."
Something eases in their shoulders. They're really talking to you now.
"Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
"Still on what day it is."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "We both stood at the treeline. Liam held it. I keep replaying my part, looking for the step I missed."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Sam nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You show them Pokeweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What? I don't know what to do with my hands today."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."

"Thanks. ...Thanks for saying that."
"The sickness took Liam. I keep washing my hands like it'll bring them back. Stupid."
"Another time. The village needs me here."

lines: d31: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Pasquale Kwiatkowski is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d31: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d31: 🕯️ Pasquale Kwiatkowski is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d31: What Pasquale kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d31: "Pasquale's gone." Liam looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Pasquale." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d31: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Alfredo blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d31: 📖 LEARNED: Pipes & Waterworks (Level 1). Water follows gravity and the path of least resistance. Find the line, find the water.
d31: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
d31: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d31: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d31: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Pasquale Kwiatkowski, 31 days. The mantle passes to Alfredo Domingo.
d31: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Alfredo Domingo, 32 — a plumber. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Bird Whisperer.
d31: The village's quarrel was with Pasquale — and Pasquale is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d31: At the grave, Sung, Ruth, Carlos and 1 more speak for Alfredo — "Pasquale trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d31: The fire knew Alfredo before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
